findings.message: This diff adds a third writer of release status: the hourly evaluateReleases. It locks rows with `for update of r`. The other two writers read the release through `tracked()`, which is a plain select with no lock: completeOnDeployment (recordDeployment) and updateRelease. They then call writeStatus, which uses the stale `r.status` for two things: the history row's from_status, and the `r.status === to` check that skips both the history row and the 127 event. As a result, release_status_history and the status_changed events can disagree with the stored status. Fix: read the release `for update` in `tracked()`, at least on the write paths, so that every writer works from the row it actually overwrites.
findings.scenario: A release is in_progress, with a target that passed yesterday. updateRelease runs at the same moment as the hourly check and moves the target 10 days out. updateRelease reads in_progress through tracked(), then blocks on the check's lock. The check writes in_progress>overdue, adds a history row, raises an event and the PM gets the Off track notice, then commits. updateRelease then sets the status to in_progress. Because its stale r.status is also in_progress, it writes no history row and raises no event. Result: the stored status is in_progress, but the last history row reads 'in_progress>overdue', and no event ever says the release came back from Off track. The same race with recordDeployment writes the history row 'in_progress>completed' and an event with from=in_progress, although the release was overdue.

findings.message: The README says the check runs 'under row locks' and that 'a second run changes nothing'. 127 says 'once per transition'. Every test runs evaluateReleases on its own, one session at a time. Delete `for update of r` and every test still passes. Add a test that runs two real sessions: two concurrent evaluateReleases runs, and the check racing recordDeployment or updateRelease. Assert one history row and one status_changed event per transition.
findings.scenario: Remove `for update of r` from release-check.ts:22. The 126 and 127 suites stay green, although two overlapping runs (for example a workflow retry after a step timeout while the first transaction still commits) would each write planned>in_progress and raise the event twice.

findings.message: `.rel-voided` sets `background:var(--warn-soft,#FFF6E0)`, but packages/ui/src/styles/tokens.css defines no `--warn-soft`. The fallback, a near-white #FFF6E0, therefore applies in every theme, while `color:var(--ink)` follows the theme. In dark theme that puts light text on a near-white background. Fix: use the existing theme-aware tokens `background:var(--chip-warn-bg);color:var(--chip-warn)`, or `var(--ink)` on `--chip-warn-bg`.
findings.rule: AGENTS core rule 8 (WCAG 2.2 AA 1.4.3, light and dark themes)
findings.scenario: Switch to dark theme and open a completed release whose completing deployment was voided. The note 'The deployment that completed this release was voided…' renders as light dark-theme ink on #FFF6E0, far below a 4.5:1 contrast ratio.

findings.message: The change treats 'failed' like 'rolled-back' in words, glyphs and logic. It misses the board track's colour: the `<li>` gets the class `failed`, and delivery.css styles only `.dv-track .rolled-back{--c:var(--chip-bad)}` (delivery.css:282). Since `--c` is unset on a failed stage, the border-top and the ✕ glyph lose the 'bad' colour. Fix: add `.dv-track .failed{--c:var(--chip-bad)}`, or render the unsuccessful state through one class.
findings.scenario: A release with Dev deployed and UAT failed appears on the project board band. The UAT segment shows a ✕ in the default text colour with no red bar, so it doesn't read as a failure, while a rolled-back UAT shows in red.

findings.message: STAGE_WORD still hard-codes 'Deployed', 'Testing' and 'Rolled back' beside the new WORD map in server/deployment-status.ts. Only 'failed' goes through StageWord. Build the map from stageWord/StageWord for every status, so the two copies can't drift. In ui/band.ts, `const STATE = (status) => stageWord(status)` is an alias that adds nothing: call stageWord directly.

evaluateReleases rebuilds what statusFor() already does (zoneOf, then releaseDay, then releaseStatus with completed:false) instead of sharing it. Fix: pull out one helper that takes the zone and the clock, and use it from both, so the check and create/update can't judge a release's day differently.

`ReleaseDeployed.status` now includes `failed`, and the README says failed and rolled-back follow one `unsuccessful` rule on every screen and read. Leave consumes this event but still tests only `a.status === "rolled-back"` (modules/leave/server/releases.ts:23). A failed deployment therefore opens the leave release window with `retry = false`, as if it had succeeded. Fix: export the `unsuccessful` rule (or a `retry` flag on the payload) through the contract so Leave can use it, and add a Leave test for a failed status.
findings.scenario: record_deployment FLT v1.8.0 UAT status=failed → leave.release_window row with retry=false; with rolled-back the same row gets retry=true

findings.message: `rolledBack` now also matches failed stages, but `stageNote` (line 42) still prints the fixed text "Rolled back from <env> on <day>". On the Overview's release-readiness card, a failed deployment reads as a rollback, although the ReleasesPage pill and the deployment chip now say "Failed". Fix: build the note from `StageWord(back.status)` and rename the helper.
findings.scenario: record_deployment CON v2.4.0 UAT status=failed → Overview readiness item note "Rolled back from UAT on Nov 26"

findings.message: The README claims the hourly check runs under row locks and that a run changes each release once. The only test runs the check twice in a row. If `for update of r` is deleted, every test still passes. Without the lock, two overlapping runs both read `planned` and both write planned→in_progress, which duplicates the history row and the `release_status_changed` event. For an Off track change, the PM gets two urgent notices. Fix: add a test that starts two `evaluateReleases` calls at once on separate connections and asserts one history row and one event.
findings.scenario: Two overlapping runs (a workflow retry while the first is still in flight, or cron fired by two workers), with the lock removed → two 'planned>overdue:schedule' rows and two Off track notifications; the current tests stay green

findings.message: The board track colours a stage by its status class. `.dv-track .rolled-back` sets `--c` to bad, but there is no rule for `.failed`. A failed stage on BoardBand gets no tone colour, so its border and glyph fall back to the ink colour. Fix: add `.dv-track .failed` to the same rule.
findings.scenario: Board for a release with UAT status failed → the UAT segment shows in ink, not in the bad tone a rolled-back segment gets

findings.message: `completingVoided` looks up the same deployment twice, through an IIFE and a non-null assertion. Look it up once (`const c = history.find(...)`) and map it.

The `ReleaseStatusChanged` contract carries display strings: `category` is a label and `targetDate` is an en-GB day label ("10 Dec 2026"), with `""` as a silent fallback. Webhook and module consumers can't parse the date, and an empty string hides a missing value. Put the ISO day and the category code in the payload, and let the notification template format them (or add separate label fields).
findings.scenario: A webhook consumer reads targetDate "30 Sept 2026" and cannot compare it with a date; a release with no target sends "" instead of null
